gaps.sentence: The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.
The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.
The suffix -en forms verbs from adjectives: thicken. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The street market sells ___ fruit in summer (JUICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -y forms the adjective: juicy fruit. A comparative or adverb cannot modify 'fruit'.

gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ of you to double-check the figures (SENSE).
gaps.explanation: 'It was sensible of you to do something' praises good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (DETERMINE) to become a doctor never wavered.
gaps.explanation: A noun is needed after 'His': determination (-ation noun); 'determined' is the adjective.
